title: curl merges about 50 bugfixes from Joshua Rogers' ZeroPath-assisted scans and by December 2025 has fixed several hundred bugs from AI analyzer reports
summary: Bug reports made mostly with the ZeroPath AI code analyzer led curl to merge about 50 fixes from a first list, and by 23 December 2025 AI analyzer reports had led to several hundred.
account: Reports to curl arrived from mid-September 2025. The curl lead maintainer, Daniel Stenberg, writes that a security report received on 16 September accurately identified a possible stack-based buffer overflow in curl's Kerberos file transfer protocol (FTP) code. It was not turned into a CVE only because the code could not be reached. The project then removed krb5-ftp support. The reporter, Joshua Rogers, then forwarded a large list of further potential issues found mostly with ZeroPath, an AI-powered code analyzer. The tool produced over two hundred possible problems despite curl's existing compilers, static analyzers and fuzzing. From the initial list about 50 separately identifiable bugfixes were merged. Stenberg told The Register on 2 October 2025 that about 50 bugfixes based on Rogers' reports had been merged. Second and third lists of 47 and 158 items followed, according to Stenberg's post of 10 October 2025. Rogers states in his retrospective of 19 October 2025 that about 98% of the curl bugs reported and fixed were discovered by ZeroPath. He puts the running total of fixed bugs around 150. In his review of 2025, published on 23 December 2025, Stenberg wrote that curl had fixed several hundred bugs as a direct result of reports from AI analyzers, primarily ZeroPath and Aisle Research.
purpose: AI-powered static analysis of source code to find vulnerabilities and bugs.
system: ZeroPath AI code analyzer (with other scanners tested by Rogers)
deployer: Joshua Rogers (independent security researcher); fixes merged by the curl project
taxonomy_note: Bugfixes rather than confirmed vulnerabilities are read as risk reduced.

ratings.reason: The curl maintainer reports that the project merged about 50 bugfixes from the first list and removed code that carried a potential overflow. By 23 December 2025 he counted several hundred bugs fixed from AI analyzer reports.
curl is widely deployed, and the sources report no averted incident that affected users. The merged fixes are described as mostly small mistakes.

ai_role.statement: The maintainer confirms the reports' quality and the merged fixes. He notes he does not know the exact split between tool and human. Rogers attributes ~98% of the fixed curl bugs to ZeroPath. Both the deployer and the confirming maintainer are independent of the vendor.

The later count of about 150 and the 98% attribution were not rechecked.

In his review of 2025, published on 23 December 2025, Stenberg wrote that curl had fixed several hundred bugs as a direct result of reports from AI analyzers, primarily ZeroPath and Aisle Research.
